LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  March 9, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:29 p.m. on March
9, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. Mayor Khan also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City
Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

In addition, Carl Petersen, Interim City Clerk, announced instructions on how to provide
live comments via Zoom and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on
all agenda items, and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the
City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Kuo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Jason Aguilar from Arise Church provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Proclaim March 2021 as “Women’s History Month”

  Mayor Khan presented a brief video on the contributions and
  accomplishments made by women throughout history and a proclamation
  recognizing March 2021 as “Women’s History Month.”

  Ray Quigley, Irvine resident, requested that the City Council meeting be
  adjourned in memory of former Irvine City Councilmember and Mayor
  John Burton.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Irvine Barclay Theatre

  Mayor Khan introduced Jerry Mandel, President, Irvine Barclay Theatre,
  who provided a brief update on the Theatre’s operations over the last
  year during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  City Council discussion included: expressing appreciation to the Irvine
  Barclay Theatre for its continued partnership and efforts during the
  COVID-19 pandemic; and suggested continued financial support for the
  Theatre during the annual budget process.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Kim recognized Irvine resident and Pacific Academy High School Senior,
  Charlotte Ding, who demonstrated strength and perseverance by becoming the youngest
  individual to climb Mount Everest at 16 years old.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  In recognition of International Women’s Day, Councilmember Kuo recognized the
  following individuals for their impact in Irvine through their leadership of non-profit
  organizations in the City:

  •  Madeleine Hernis, CEO, Families Forward
  •  Jerri Rosen, Founder/CEO, Working Wardrobes
  •  Yulan Chung, Principal/Executive Director, Irvine Chinese School and
  South Coast Chinese Cultural Center
  •  Tilly Levine, Co-Founder, Tilly’s Retail Center and Tilly’s Life Center
  •  Kimberly Beeson, Executive Director, Irvine Adult Day Health Services
  •  Patricia Wenskunas, Founder/CEO, Crime Survivors
  •  Sharon Wellikson, Executive Director, Irvine Children’s Fund
  •  Neda Eaton, President/CEO, Irvine Public Schools Foundation

  Councilmember Agran noted his recent attendance at the March 3 Air Quality
  Management District meeting regarding the All American Asphalt plant; and that he had
  received several calls regarding the status of the Veterans’ Cemetery, suggesting
  collaboration with the Mayor to agendize his proposed resolution in support of the
  Amended and Restated Development Agreement (ARDA) site as the preferred site for
  the Veterans’ Cemetery.

  Councilmember Carroll noted that the Orange County Power Authority (OCPA) held an
  in-depth special meeting regarding an “Energy 101 Workshop,” where the OCPA
  featured leaders of Community Choice Aggregation entities throughout the State of
  California; and urged the public to view the recording at ocpower.org to learn more about
  the Community Choice Energy program.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  The Emergency Rental Assistance Program was launched on March 8, 2021, to
  help mitigate the impacts of COVID-19 on Irvine’s residential renters. The City has
  allocated approximately $17.7 million for the program, which is funded through a
  combination of federal and state dollars. The program will help keep residents in
  their homes by providing relief for those who have been adversely affected by the
  pandemic and will provide funding for unpaid rent from April 1, 2021, to March 31,
  2021. The OC United Way will be administering the Emergency Rental Assistance
  Program for the City and the application period will close on March 19 at 5 p.m. To
  ensure all residents are reached, the City is conducting outreach in Chinese,
  English, Farsi, Korean, Spanish and Vietnamese. Information on the program can
  be found in each of these languages on the City’s website and on social media.
  After the application period has closed, a lottery system will be used to select grant
  recipients, in order to provide equitable access for all Irvine renters. For eligibility
  information in English, Chinese, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese, and Farsi, visit
  cityofirvine.org/erap.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  •  The community is invited to join City staff on Thursday, March 11, at 4 p.m. to learn
  more about the 2021-23 budget and provide their input. This will be the first of two
  virtual Community Budget Workshops. The virtual meetings will be held via Zoom
  and Facebook Live, and will include a presentation and answers to question about
  the budget. To register for the workshop, visit cityofirvine.org. Questions and
  comments regarding the budget can be emailed to budget@cityofirvine.org ahead
  of the meeting. The second workshop will be held on March 25 at 9 a.m.

  •  Earlier this month, construction began on the highly anticipated Bommer Canyon
  Cattle Camp Rehabilitation Project. The Cattle Camp area is undergoing upgrades
  and renovations to improve and update the event site and surrounding park
  grounds, a 15-acre site originally built in 1967. New facilities at Cattle Camp, which
  has been a popular spot for community parties, picnics, weddings, and campouts,
  will match the park’s original ranch style. The project includes constructing new
  buildings, a “chuckwagon” building and stage, and new ADA accessible pathways.
  A new waterline being brought to the property will allow for construction of a new
  restroom building. Cattle Camp is closed to the public during construction, and
  access to nearby trails and parking may be closed intermittently throughout
  construction of the project. The project is expected to be completed this year. For
  additional information on the Camp Cattle project, visit cityofirvine.org/cattlecamp.

  •  The Irvine Animal Care Center invites the community to support its Foster Donation
  Drive, taking place through March 31. The community can support the center’s
  new puppies, kittens, and young rabbits, as well as recuperating animals, by
  donating supplies such as formula, towels, and toys. For a complete wish list, visit
  irvineanimals.org. The community can also support the Foster Care program at a
  Drive-Thru Donation Celebration on Sunday, March 21 from 3 to 4 p.m. by driving
  through the center’s parking lot to drop off new pet supplies to support puppies
  and kittens in foster care. Community members can place supplies from the wish
  list in their trunks, stay in their vehicles, wear a mask, and Irvine Animal Care
  Center staff will unload the items. The Center’s Foster Care program provides a
  home environment, supplies, food, and veterinary care for animals too young to be
  adopted, and those recovering from medical procedures. Members of the public
  interested in providing temporary care for young kittens, puppies, and rabbits, or
  animals recovering from a medical procedure, can learn more at
  irvineanimals.org/foster.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  3.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Carroll, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim,
  and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.1, 3.2, 3.3,
  and 3.5. Consent Calendar Item No. 3.4 was removed for separate
  discussion.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  3.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of the special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on February 9, 2021.
  2) Approved the minutes of the regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on February 9, 2021.

  3.2  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 21-09 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND
  SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO
  BE PAID

  3.3  UPDATES TO CITYWIDE RECORDS RETENTION SCHEDULE

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 21-10 – A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  ADOPTING  THE  CITYWIDE  RECORDS  RETENTION
  SCHEDULE AND SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION NO. 18-84

  3.4  AMENDMENT OF THE BYLAWS OF THE GREEN RIBBON
  ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of
  Councilmember Kuo, who suggested a revision to the bylaws requiring
  that voting members be of high school age rather than middle school
  through high school age.

  City Council discussion included: noting why the Green Ribbon
  Environmental Committee had recommended middle school aged
  members; inquired about whether term limits had been established for
  youth members; noted potential scheduling conflicts for middle school
  aged members; and requested a modification to the section on
  guidelines for students.

  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the proposed
  amendments to the Green Ribbon Environmental Committee bylaws.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Mayor Khan, to:

  Adopt - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE POWERS,
  DUTIES, AND BYLAWS OF THE IRVINE GREEN RIBBON
  ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE as amended per the errata
  memo dated March 9, 2021, and to include the following
  modification:

  Section 2(d): “…however, youth At-Large members shall
  serve one-year terms.”

  ACTION: A friendly amendment was made by Vice Mayor Kim,
  accepted by Councilmember Kuo as the maker of the motion and
  Mayor Khan as the seconder, and unanimously carried to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 21-11 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  AMENDING THE POWERS, DUTIES, AND BYLAWS OF THE
  IRVINE GREEN RIBBON ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE as
  amended per the errata memo dated March 9, 2021, and to
  include the following modifications:

  1) Section 2(d): “…however, youth At-Large members shall
  serve one-year terms.”
  2) Section 2(e) to include: “Personal engagement in
  environmental volunteer activities, or efforts to raise
  awareness on environmental issues.”

  3.5  FIRST AMENDMENT TO LEASE AGREEMENT WITH NATIONAL
  RAILROAD PASSENGER CORPORATION

  ACTION:
  Approved a First Amendment to Lease Agreement with National
  Railroad Passenger Corporation and authorize the Interim City
  Manager or her designee to execute the attached First
  Amendment. (Contract No. 4091A)

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  4.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  4.1  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE AND DIRECTION TO DIRECTOR
  OF EMERGENCY SERVICES ON RELEVANT ACTION ITEMS,
  INCLUDING CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH CUROGRAM FOR
  COVID-19 TESTING SERVICES THROUGH MAY 27, 2021

  Melissa Haley, Deputy City Manager, presented the staff report.

  There was no City Council discussion.

  There were no public comments.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Kim, and unanimously carried to:

  1) Extend all previously issued City orders and resolutions
  related to COVID-19 through at least May 12, 2021.
  2) Authorize the Interim City Manager to extend the contract
  for public and employee COVID-19 testing services with
  Curogram, Inc. through May 27, 2021 for an amount not-
  to-exceed $33,200 as amended per the errata memo
  dated March 8, 2021. (Contract No. 11089J)

  4.2  AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR PUBLIC SAFETY BODY-WORN
  CAMERA AND MOBILE VIDEO SYSTEM SOLUTION

  Mike Hamel, Chief of Police/Director of Public Safety, and Jade Mazzio,
  Business Services Manager, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included: discussing video retention and whether
  indefinite storage/retention would be an option; noted that body-worn
  cameras would build community trust; inquired about who was
  responsible for the pre- and post-implementation of the body-worn
  cameras; questioned how and where the data would be stored; inquired
  about the process for additional storage data if data limits were
  exceeded; inquired about video resolution and camera features, such as
  mute mode functionality and auto activation capabilities; expressed
  concern about privacy with respect to sexual assault and domestic
  violence victims; suggested community outreach to inform the members
  of the public about the implementation of body-worm cameras;
  referenced roundtable discussions related to body-worn cameras with
  community members following the Black Lives Matter events last year;
  suggested that body-worn cameras would hold police officers
  accountable; and reiterated that body-cameras would effectively

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  demonstrate that police department employees practice community
  policing, de-escalation, and non-lethal techniques.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the body-worn cameras
  and related funding from the Strategic Technology Plan budget, and
  suggested reallocation of Irvine Police Department funding to other
  community programs:

  •  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident
  •  Charlotte Kings
  •  Alejandro Sobrera
  •  Dinorah Hernandez, UCI student
  •  Justin Fong, UCI student
  •  Sylvester Ani, Irvine resident
  •  Elena Bock, UCI student
  •  Stephen Coffey, UCI student

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine high school student, spoke in support of the body-
  worn cameras, and referenced the support received for such cameras
  following the community protests that occurred last year.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Kim, and unanimously carried to:

  1) Award a contract to Axon Enterprise, Inc. in the amount not to
  exceed $3,312,024.76 over 5 fiscal years. (Contract No.
  11278)
  2) Authorized the Mayor to execute the contract between Axon
  Enterprise, Inc. and the City of Irvine.

  4.3  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR KHAN, VICE MAYOR
  KIM, AND COUNCILMEMBERS AGRAN, CARROLL, AND KUO, TO
  ADOPT A RESOLUTION FOR THE CONVENTION ON THE
  ELIMINATION OF ALL FORMS OF DISCRIMINATION AGAINST
  WOMEN

  The item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan, and co-
  sponsored by Vice Mayor Kim and Councilmembers Agran, Carroll, and
  Kuo, who suggested City Council adoption of a resolution for the
  convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against
  women.

  City Council discussion included: expressing concern that some
  language was directive; and inquired about whether expenditures would
  be tracked with respect to staff time implementing the resolution.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  8
 City Council Minutes  March 9, 2021

  The following individuals spoke in support on the adoption of the
  resolution:

  •  Rima Nashashibi
